description: Short decorative cast lamp post with a fluted shaft and a lantern head, of the kind lining riverside and old-town promenades

image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Short decorative lamp post standing on a stepped square plinth, its shaft swelling into a moulded collar at the bottom and rising as a fluted column with shallow vertical grooves, a ring of moulded banding partway up, and on top a single lantern head built as a tapering six-sided glazed box with solid corner posts and a solid moulded cap above it finished with a small pointed finial Materials: Dark bottle-green cast paint over metal, chalky and sun-bleached on one side with fine crazing, rust weeping from the plinth bolts and the base collar, dust and cobwebs in the flutes, glazing panels grimy and clouded with insect debris.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless pure WHITE studio matte. The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless white backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.925 carried from the recorded review; the neck lathe added ~100 triangles. 5/6 draw calls, 3/4 materials, 5/8 unique geometries.

featureReviews.evidence: Measured bbox 0.400 x 4.085 x 0.400 m against the corrected declaration of 0.42 x 4.2 x 0.42 -- 4.8% under on width and depth, 2.7% on height. The declaration was corrected from 0.55 on a hue-mask profile of the plate: plinth 0.327 of height, lantern 0.286, ratio 0.874 against the asset notes' 0.35/0.40. Unchanged by v3.

The post changes section as the plate does: a SQUARE four-step plinth, a ROUND fluted column, a two-step square abacus, a ROUND moulded neck (v3), and the SQUARE lantern. The neck is the plate's drum between abacus and sill; v2 skipped it and the lantern floated 13 cm above the abacus.

A frame of four corner posts between a sill and a cornice with warm glazing recessed inside them, under a square pyramid roof and a two-part spike finial -- now standing on the neck drum, which starts 5 mm inside the abacus top and flares into the brass band and sill.
Every tone solved against gatecrop's erased 55.5-60.5 window: cast iron darkened to luma 48 (lit mouldings 52), brass lifted to 124. The neck carries the lit-moulding tone. Unchanged.
Four brass knobs instanced at the cornice corners at +-0.175 m, outboard of the roof slope. Unchanged.

name: Ornamental Lamp Post

notes:
The decorative post used along Chao Phraya promenades, Rattanakosin footpaths and municipal park frontages -- much shorter than a road lighting column and read at pedestrian distance, so the moulded collar, flutes and lantern cap all have to be real geometry rather than texture. Sized from a 4 m mounting height; the plinth is about 0.4 m square and the lantern head about 0.35 m across. budgetClass is the derived large, which is right: the lantern head is the only expensive part and its six sides are one lathed or instanced form. Static: bolted to a plinth, so physics stays disabled.

BUDGET CLASS RAISED large -> hero (2026-08-31), one step, as part of the lighting-kit rebuild to a fidelity above 0.92. The lighting props were authored to ceilings that could not carry their identity features -- the bulkhead's guard cage is the clearest case: as one lathe inside 800 triangles the only guard expressible is two circumferential bands, and it rendered as a stack of pale discs. The extra room is a CEILING, not a target: every one of these is still built by merging parts into as few components as possible, so draw calls, materials and unique geometries stay far below the new class and only triangles are actually spent.

WIDTH AND DEPTH CORRECTED 2026-08-31, 0.55 -> 0.42 m, from the plate and this entry's own notes agreeing against the declared figure. Masking the plate by hue (the prop is green cast iron, brass and glass against a NEUTRAL GREY GRADIENT backdrop, so a luma sweep test fails on it and a hue test does not) profiles the subject at 319 x 976 px: the plinth is the widest thing at 0.327 of the height, the column runs 0.121 and the lantern-and-roof 0.286. Those PROPORTIONS confirm the notes exactly -- lantern/plinth measures 0.874 against the notes' 0.35/0.40 = 0.875 -- while the plate's absolute scale does not, since at the declared 4.2 m height its plinth would be 1.37 m. So the notes' 0.40 m plinth is right and it is the widest part of the prop, which puts the envelope at 0.42 including the base step, not 0.55. Nothing on this post is 0.55 m across.
